messages:
simon: heads up — CI perf regression on the small-batch latency job after the driver image bump (driver 545.87 -> 546.12). spike shows up only on nvlink nodes.

anika: saw this too, noticed p95 went from ~42ms -> ~95ms for batch size 2. failing test: runtime/smoke/small-batch-latency.

leo: logs look like kernel choose moved from `fast_attention_kernel_v2` -> `attention_fallback_kernel` for 16/32 seq lengths. odd because inputs didn't change.

perfbot: perf CI: job runtime/smoke/small-batch-latency failed (p95 +127%). Attach: /artifacts/perf/1891234567/prof.tar.gz

anika: pastable profiler snippet (from repro VM):
```
Device: A100-SXM4
Kernel times (ms):
 fast_attention_kernel_v2  : 0.45
 attention_fallback_kernel : 1.12  <-- 2.5x slower
 matmul_tile_kernel        : 0.12
 total inference step      : 3.9ms -> 8.6ms
```

tess: @simon did we change kernel selection heuristics recently? There was a change to favor more numerically stable kernels on new drivers.

simon: we merged a Triton / kernel-dispatch tweak (PR #3721) last week that adjusted heuristics for sequence < 64 to prefer fusion-safe kernels. I didn't think driver would flip it back this way.

leo: running a quick bisect locally — toggling the heuristic flag `prefer_fused_attention=false` reverts to `fast_attention_kernel_v2` and latency drops back.

oncall: rolling canary for the driver image is paused. this is a rollout blocker until root cause is clear.

anika: can we capture cuobjdump / kernel name signatures for both kernels? suspect driver changed PTX-to-SASS scheduling causing the dispatch decision to think fused kernel is not supported.

perfbot: perf trace (light):
`dispatch_kernel(attn): reason=heuristic_score(0.42) -> chose fallback`
`heuristic: supports_fusion=false because cuobj attributes mismatch`

simon: created a quick revert branch that forces `prefer_fused_attention=true` at runtime. running CI now. If that fixes CI we can ship a targeted fix to selection logic.

leo: repro shows that NV driver 546.* returns different `sm_arch` capability flags for our container kernel query. wonder if the driver changed the exposed attribute name.

tess: open question — should we make selection robust against missing attributes (i.e., fallback to capability-mask table) or pin to kernel version? leaning to make selection tolerant.

anika: for immediate mitigation, can we add a server-side override to force fused kernels for models tagged `small-batch-optimized`? then we can continue rollout.

simon: agree. I'll push a hotfix flag and coordinate with infra to patch canary nodes. @release-bot please hold any further driver image merges.

release-bot: paused driver-image rollouts; blocking PRs: driver-image-update-546.12.

leo: CI on revert branch is green for the latency job. still running full perf suite.

oncall: after hotfix we should run a quick full-matrix test across smaller seq lengths and different GPU SKUs (A100, H100). NVLink seems to exacerbate it.

anika: adding a small perf test to nightly matrix that asserts kernel choice stability across driver minor versions. will add a noisy log when selection flips.

simon: good. follow-ups: (1) harden selection logic to not rely on a single driver attribute, (2) add telemetry for kernel-choice deltas so we can alert on unexpected swaps, (3) patch canary nodes with override until fixed.

tess: thanks all. I'll coordinate infra rollout pause and schedule a quick postmortem doc after we confirm root cause.

leo: FYI — I'll also open an upstream triton/dispatch issue with reproduction details and cuobjdiffs.

simon: ok closing loop here, will post updates in this thread as CI completes.

perfbot: CI revert branch perf: small-batch-latency p95 returned to baseline (within 3%).
